events.description:
Back on Calendar
 
Date/Time: Held on the 2nd Saturday of each month, beginning at Sunset. Cancellations due to weather may occur.

The OakOasis Star Party is a family event great for Astronomers and Earthlings of all sizes. We have a variety of activities all about the night sky. The evening often begins with a twilight hike to check out some bats and scorpions while we wait for the stars to arrive. Once we get back to the parking area, we begin looking at the stars and planets through telescopes. The Park Ranger and SDAA volunteers orient people to the night sky by pointing out planets and constellations and teaching basic astronomy.

events.title: Lunar Eclipse at The Fleet
events.description:
Fleet Science Center Special Event:
This Lunar Eclipse happens to occur on a "Supermoon", when the Moon is at perigee, closest to Earth in it's orbit. After January 20, the next total lunar eclipse will be on May 26, 2021. Check out the following link for some great information about Lunar Eclipses:
https://www.timeanddate.com/eclipse/total-lunar-eclipse.html

Tonight, The Fleet has a special program set up with Astronomer Lisa Will, inside the planetarium. We will host the observing session with binoculars and scopes in the area of the fountain, in front of the Fleet Science Center. Our tentative schedule will be:


4:53 PM; Moon rise, SDAA setup
6:36 PM; Penumbral, feint eclipse begins
7:33 PM; Umbral, full eclipse begins
8:41 to 9:43; Time of Totality
10:00 PM; SDAA hosting ends


The Fleet website has posted their promotional and ticket information at:https://www.rhfleet.org/events/sky-tonight-special-lunar-eclipse

events.title: Lunar Eclipse
events.description:
In San Diego the Moon will rise on Sunday, 5-15-2022, at 7:32 PM.
At that time the eclipse will be in progress in the "partial phase" and will be located in the East-South-Eastern sky at an azimuth of 113 Deg. The Progress of the Moon will follow the night time ecliptic which is very low in the Southern sky as we approach the Summer Solstice.
 
Here is a chart of the eclipse progress from the Timeanddate.com website:
 
EventUTC TimeTime in San Diego*Visible in San Diego
Penumbral Eclipse beginsMay 16 at 01:32:05May 15 at 6:32:05 pmNo, below the horizon
Partial Eclipse beginsMay 16 at 02:27:52May 15 at 7:27:52 pmNo, below the horizon
Full Eclipse beginsMay 16 at 03:29:03May 15 at 8:29:03 pmYes
Maximum EclipseMay 16 at 04:11:28May 15 at 9:11:28 pmYes
Full Eclipse endsMay 16 at 04:53:55May 15 at 9:53:55 pmYes
Partial Eclipse endsMay 16 at 05:55:07May 15 at 10:55:07 pmYes
Penumbral Eclipse endsMay 16 at 06:50:49May 15 at 11:50:49 pmYes

* The Moon is below the horizon in San Diego some of the time, so that part of the eclipse is not visible.

Find a location with a clear view to the SE horizon and watch this early evening event.
 
The SDAA will be providing a live video feed to the Timeanddate.com website and their YouTube channel, hopefully, depending on local weather and internet access. Here is the link to the Timeanddate.com feed:
 
https://www.timeanddate.com/live/eclipse-lunar-2022-may-16
events.location: San Diego, CA (or any location with SE horizon view)

events.description:
THIS IS AN IN PERSON MEETING AT MTRP VISITOR'S CENTER.               

Topic: Astronomical Word Play

Speaker: Dr. Richard Lederer

Our speaker is the distinguished verbavore Dr. Richard Lederer, who is an American linguist, author, speaker, and teacher. He is best known for his books on the English language and on wordplay such as puns, oxymorons, and anagrams. He has been dubbed âthe Wizard of Idiom,â âAttila the Pun,â and âConan the Grammarian.â He will focus on astronomical terminology and language as only he can.

This will be an in-person program meeting at Mission Trails Regional Park.
